about.title: Hanford Wrongful Death Claims
about.longDescription: Kings County recorded no traffic deaths inside Hanford in 2025, which is good news for a city of about 55,000 people. It also means that when a family here does lose someone — whether on N 11th Avenue, at a job site, in a hospital, or in a fall that should never have happened — the loss feels especially out of place. The same year saw 80 injury collisions and 107 people hurt, a reminder that serious crashes still happen here. California law lets a surviving spouse or domestic partner and children bring a wrongful death claim first, with certain dependents and heirs able to step in when there is no one in that first group. The claim is civil and moves on its own track, apart from any criminal charges. Most families have two years from the date of death to file, and far less if a city, county, or state agency is involved. We handle wrongful death cases on a contingency basis, so there is no fee unless you recover.

items.title: Clarity on who may file
items.desc: California limits standing to a spouse or domestic partner and children first, then certain dependents and heirs. We will sort out who belongs on the claim before anything is filed.

items.title: Deadlines handled early
items.desc: The general two-year window runs from the date of death, and claims involving a government entity close much sooner. Getting involved early protects your family's options.

items.title: A civil case, on its own track
items.desc: A wrongful death claim is separate from any criminal proceeding and seeks funeral and burial costs, lost financial support, and the loss of love, companionship, and guidance. We work on contingency, so there is no fee unless there is a recovery.

items.question: Hanford had no traffic deaths in 2025 — do wrongful death claims still happen here?
items.answer: They do. Wrongful death covers any death caused by another party's negligence or wrongdoing, not only crashes, so claims in Kings County often stem from workplace incidents, medical neglect, unsafe property, or defective products. And with 80 injury collisions on Hanford roads that same year, a fatal crash on a busy stretch like 11th Avenue remains possible in any given year.

items.question: My sibling died and had no spouse or children. Can I bring a claim?
items.answer: Possibly. California gives first priority to a spouse or domestic partner and children, but when none exist, certain dependents and heirs under the intestate succession rules may have standing. We will review your family situation to confirm who qualifies.

items.question: The other driver is facing criminal charges. Do we have to wait for that case to end?
items.answer: No. A wrongful death claim is a civil action and proceeds separately from any criminal case, with its own rules and its own two-year filing deadline. Waiting for a criminal verdict can put that deadline at risk, especially if a public agency is involved and the window is shorter.
